patient preferences for choice and participation in health care decisions are strongly linked to the age of the individual patient.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients in general want to be informed and to have the opportunity to make their own choices, but that the degree of participation is dependent on a number of factors such as age, gender, health status, and expectations.
patients are not only interested in choice and shared decision, but also in being able to participate in health care in a way that suits their needs.
patient preferences for choice and participation in decision making depend on the patients' own health status and the expected future health care needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patient views are complex and cannot easily be reduced to a single dimension, such as the degree of patient involvement.
patient preferences are highly heterogeneous, and that the design of health care services needs to be adapted to individual preferences.
